problem: Find a parametric equation of the plane that passes through the points $A(3,1,5),\,B(6,-8,0)$, and $C(-2,1,3).$
worked_solution:
First, we need to find two vectors that are parallel to the plane (but not to each other). Let's use the displacement vectors $\overset{\to }{AB}$ and $\overset{\to }{AC},$ as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}\overset{\to }{AB} & =⟨6,-8,0⟩-⟨3,1,5⟩ \\  & =⟨3,-9,-5⟩ \\ \overset{\to }{AC} & =⟨-2,1,3⟩-⟨3,1,5⟩ \\  & =⟨-5,0,-2⟩\end{aligned}
$$

Now, if we consider the position vector $a=⟨3,1,5⟩$ of the point $A,$ then the corresponding parametric equation of the plane is given by

$$
\begin{aligned}r & =a+s\overset{\to }{AB}+t\overset{\to }{AC} \\ r & =⟨3,1,5⟩+s⟨3,-9,-5⟩+t⟨-5,0,-2⟩,\,s,t\in (-\infty ,\infty ).\end{aligned}
$$
